newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND NEEDS PLN 4.8 BLN TO REPAIR ENVIRONMENT.
newsitem.headline: POLAND NEEDS PLN 4.8 BLN TO REPAIR ENVIRONMENT.

text.p: Poland will need about 4.8 billion zlotys to repair environmental damage caused by July's catastrophic flooding and mend flood defences, the environmental protection ministry said on Thursday.

The ministry said in a statement that the sum, to be spent until 2010, would be needed to repair retention reservoirs and dams, return rivers to their beds, mend sewage systems, detoxicate soil poisoned by damaged sewage plants and chemical waste dumps, and for other expenses.
Forest damage alone amounts to 240 million zlotys, PAP quoted State Forest Agency head Janusz Dawidziuk as saying.

Total damage remains unknown, but some independent analysts have estimated it at up to 7.5 billion zlotys. The Central Statistical Office (GUS) says the first tentative estimates will be possible in mid-August.

Transport Minister Boguslaw Liberadzki said on Thursday that about 200 million zlotys would be needed make roads and railways usable. Much more will be needed to fully repair the road and rail system and rebuild bridges, he said.
Liberadzki told a news conference that out of more than 3,000 km of roads affected by the floods, 1,230 km remained unpassable.
The southwestern province of Legnica, one of more than a dozen of provinces hit by the flood, estimated its damage at 203 million zlotys. Other provinces have not given their estimates.
The agriculture ministry has estimated that grain losses may amount to 600,000 to 800,000 tonnes.
Analysts estimate Poland's 1997 grain output at between 23.6 between 24.7 million tonnes. In 1996, Poland produced 24.7 million tonnes of grain.
The floods, which hit southwestern Poland nearly four weeks ago, killed 54 people and swamped more than 6,000 sq km including several big cities. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
